hypotheses.paper: G acts by morphisms of topological spacetimes
hypotheses.note: DEC-12: each g • · a strong morphism; each g is then an isomorphism
ChartIso, equivalent to strong morphism of the subspaces with strong-morphism inverse (chartIso_iff_strongMorphism), DEC-12

hypotheses.paper: uniqueness among causalities making every chart of the maximal atlas an isomorphism
hypotheses.note: false as stated (GX_maximal_not_unique, ℝ ⊔ ℝ); holds outright when some chart of the maximal atlas covers M (existsUnique_causality_GX_of_covering_chart); in general proved among absolutely minimal causalities (existsUnique_causality_GX_maximal)

findings: ETT.tex:592-594, uniqueness, under DEC-16's maximal atlas: FALSE as stated in the library's reading, TRUE outright when some chart of the maximal atlas covers M. Counterexample (GX_maximal_not_unique): M = ℝ ⊔ ℝ, X = ℝ with the timelike line, G = translations. Every chart of the maximal atlas is, along each copy, a single translation onto ℝ, so none is injective on all of M (twoLines_source_ne_univ). The absolutely minimal causality C has ¬ (inl 1 ≤_M inl 0) (twoLines_not_le), and C.topEnlarge (≤_M enlarged to all pairs, non-local by kb/0014) still makes every chart of the maximal atlas an isomorphism, since no chart sees M itself. The defect is in the claimed equivalence of the 'Equivalently' form of defi:causalite (ETT.tex:237, implemented without gluing) with the sheaf form, not in the proposition: under gluing (≤ generated by covers, i.e. absolute minimality) uniqueness holds, which is what the proof's last sentence ('minimality gives uniqueness', ETT.tex:613) establishes (existsUnique_causality_GX_maximal). The earlier interval witness (GX_not_unique_without_minimality) used a non-maximal atlas and disappears under DEC-16, the identity of ℝ forcing timelikeLine (eq_of_chartIso_refl). Not settled: connected M covered by no chart (e.g. a cylinder); on the timelike circle ≤_M is already total, so the enlargement there changes nothing.

ETT.tex:606-608, hypothesis (B): 'transition maps are restrictions of elements of G, hence the transported causalities agree on overlaps' is immediate only if each transition is the restriction of ONE element of G on the whole overlap. In the usual definition the element is constant only on components (or, in the groupoid reading, only locally), and then agreement on an open subset of the overlap needs a relation there to be a chain of local relations: absolute minimality of the model on every open subset, which (A)'s argument (rem:cac_local + cor:causalement_connexe_minimal) supplies. Lean: compatible_of_agree_locally.
ETT.tex:609-611, (C): the Baire property of X and its locality are not needed (OQ-10).
Analyticity of (G,X) is used nowhere in the proof.

The produced causality is, by construction, the one generated by the transported chart causalities (Causality.generated); cor:massA_cac (ETT.tex:1408-1416) relies on this, and it is what the Lean existence witness is.
questions: Uniqueness: is the sheaf clause of defi:causalite meant as gluing (then 'unique' is right and the 'Equivalently' form needs the gluing axiom, kb/0014), or should the statement say 'unique absolutely minimal'? Under DEC-16 the gap is exactly the manifolds no chart covers (GX_maximal_not_unique on ℝ ⊔ ℝ).
Is M assumed connected in prop:GX_espace_temps_topo? The counterexample is disconnected; the connected uncovered case is not settled here.

labels.label: prop:GX_sing_espace_temps_topo

hypotheses.note: abstracted: model X with G acting; model spaces Y α with causalities; charts r α k of reg(Y α) into X; an atlas of M with charts eX i into X and eY j into Y (β j); transitions locally (hXX) an element of G, (hXY) an element of G followed by the inverse of a regular chart, (hYY) a LOCAL isomorphism of model spaces: an open partial homeomorphism between model spaces which is a ChartIso (a global ModelIso is the special case agreeOn_of_modelIso). Analyticity not used. The model spaces of Section 3 are not built.

hypotheses.paper: (a) X causally arc-connected, G acts by morphisms
(b) the causality of X_α extends the natural causality of reg(X_α)
hypotheses.note: every regular chart r α k is a ChartIso from Y α to X; since Y α is absolutely minimal on every open subset this is equivalent to its restriction to reg being the causality prop:GX_espace_temps_topo gives
proved among absolutely minimal causalities; false as stated already in the case J = ∅ (GX_maximal_not_unique)

hypotheses.paper: the atlas A of the (G,X,X_A)-manifold (maximal, DEC-16)
hypotheses.note: stated over a given atlas; the abstracted data have no single structure groupoid whose maximal atlas could be taken; a further compatible chart is an isomorphism by the argument of chartIso_of_mem_maximalAtlas (not repeated)

findings: ETT.tex:628-632: the second half of (b) ('extends the natural causality of reg(X_α)') is needed at (B) and not cited there. The proof cites (a) and (b) for (A), where causal arc-connectedness of X_α suffices, and cites only 'restrictions of elements of G and of isomorphisms of the model spaces' for (B). The transitions between a chart into X and a chart into X_α are neither; they are (G,X)-charts of reg(X_α) composed with elements of G, and agreement across them is exactly (b)'s second half (Lean: agreeOn_of_regular).
Uniqueness: as for prop:GX_espace_temps_topo, false in the gluing-free 'Equivalently' form, true under the gluing reading (absolute minimality).
(C) Baire not needed (OQ-10); analyticity not used.
'Analytic singular structure', '(G,X,X_A)-manifold', reg(X_α) and its (G,X)-structure are used but not defined in this paper (cited to the thesis).

Non-vacuity: causality_singularGX_line states the hypotheses of existsUnique_causality_singularGX, instantiated, as conjuncts, for M = ℝ with two model spaces, a regular chart with target ]0,∞[ ≠ X, one X-chart on ]0,∞[ and two Y-charts on ]-∞,1[ (overlaps ]0,1[ and ]-∞,1[), and proves the produced causality is the timelike line.
questions: What exactly is a (G,X,X_A)-manifold? Taken: charts into X or into some X_α; transitions locally elements of G (X–X), isomorphisms of model spaces (X_α–X_β), or an element of G composed with a (G,X)-chart of reg(X_α) (X–X_α). Is an X_α–X_β transition with α ≠ β allowed, and are 'isomorphisms of model spaces' global isomorphisms X_α → X_β (as taken) or local ones?
(b) 'whose causality extends the natural causality of reg(X_α)': taken as 'every (G,X)-chart of reg(X_α) is an isomorphism of topological spacetimes'. Confirm.

labels.label: rem:hypotheses_proposition_prop_gx

hypotheses.note: unbranched and at regular points only: strongMorphism_of_gxMorphism needs, at every point of the source, a chart into X on both sides in which the map reads as an element of G; singular points (charts into X_α) and branch points are not covered
the source causality absolutely minimal and the charts of both sides isomorphisms (true of the causality the proposition produces)

findings: 'Branched (G,X)-morphism' is not defined in the paper and the remark gives no proof. Proved for unbranched maps at regular points only: an open continuous map which reads, near every point, in charts into X, as an element of G is a strong morphism when the source causality is absolutely minimal (strongMorphism_of_gxMorphism; general form strongMorphism_of_locally). At singular and branch points the argument says nothing.
questions: Define 'branched (G,X)-morphism' (open? a (G,X)-morphism on the regular parts and continuous?), and say whether 'morphism' is strong or weak.

kb_proposals: theo:causalite_engendre with (B) asked LOCALLY: existsUnique_absolutelyMinimal_of_agree_locally (GXStructure) — causalities absolutely minimal on every open subset of their domains and agreeing near each point of the overlaps glue to a unique absolutely minimal causality. Use it for any locally-modelled space instead of re-proving Compatible.

A causality given by a chart into a model: Causality.chartTransport D e, with ChartIso (relational isomorphism, equivalent to DEC-10's by chartIso_iff_strongMorphism); ChartIso.absolutelyMinimalOn transports absolute minimality from the model.
Two Causality values are equal once their toPrecausality are: Causality.ext_toPrecausality (cases/cases/rfl fails when one side is a defined term).

OpenPartialHomeomorph composition: write e.symm.trans e', the notation ≫ₕ needs `open OpenPartialHomeomorph`/`Manifold`. HasGroupoid.compatible needs (G := …) explicitly or instance synthesis is stuck.
A ChartedSpace given as a def must be @[reducible] (kb/0004); use it with @atlas ℝ _ ℝ _ inst and @HasGroupoid ℝ _ ℝ _ inst G.

Maximal atlas (DEC-16): chartIso_of_mem_maximalAtlas — an absolutely minimal causality with every atlas chart an isomorphism makes every maximal-atlas chart one; absolutelyMinimalOn_of_locally upgrades global absolute minimality to every open set when it holds hereditarily near each point. Uniqueness without minimality holds outright when a chart of the maximal atlas covers M and can fail otherwise: Causality.topEnlarge is the generic non-local witness.
